subject: May billing — unexpected peak around daily rollover; request for smoothing credit and VAT treatment

Subject: Overages on May invoice around daily rollover — asking for smoothing credit

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. We reviewed our May invoice and see a ~2.8% bump in token count that consistently appears right at the UTC daily rollover (23:59–00:01 UTC). It looks like a small handful of high-throughput sessions are being double-counted during the hourly rollup. We pulled a few sample traces and attached a CSV with the timestamps (usage_samples_202605.csv).

We’d like Redwood to:
- Confirm if there was any change to metering/aggregation logic in May (we weren’t notified of anything);
- Provide an explanation for the rollover-aligned spikes; and
- Propose a smoothing/retroactive credit for the portion of usage that appears to be measurement noise.

Because we operate across EU regions and handle VAT reporting tightly, please also confirm how any retro credit will be reflected on the invoice (gross vs net and VAT treatment).

We’ve paused our month-end payment hold pending this clarification. Happy to hop on a 30 min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alicia Romero
Head of Platform Ops
MerchantCo

Hi all — quick update from the forensics side after a first-pass investigation.

What I looked at: the sample timestamps Alicia sent + our ingestion ledger and prefixed-session registry.
Findings (summary):
- There was no global change to the metering algorithm in May; rollout logs show no config flips in the billing pipeline for MerchantCo.
- We do see ~0.9–3.4% of sessions that have two ingest events within a 90s window straddling 23:58–00:02 UTC. Those correlate with short-lived client reconnections.
- Root cause hypothesis: an upstream SDK (client-side) auto-reconnect + our per-session ephemeral key rotation produced duplicate session-start events for a subset of requests at the daily boundary. The ingestion dedupe window was 60s; some clients reconnected after ~70–80s, producing second-start events that we currently count as separate sessions.
- Impact: for MerchantCo’s May usage, this pattern maps to approximately 2.3% of billed tokens (per our sampling).

Proposed remediation & credit path:
1) Technical: we’ll extend the dedupe window for MerchantCo’s tenant to 120s for backfill reprocessing and mark duplicates as non-billable (no change to live dedupe for others).
2) Credit calculation: apply a 2.3% smoothing credit to the May invoice token line-item; we’ll calculate token->monetary value using the same per-token rate used on the invoice (no discounting).
3) Accounting: create an invoice credit memo and a corrected invoice reflecting the net amount.
4) VAT: Marissa should confirm whether the credit memo will carry VAT reversal or a net reduction depending on MerchantCo’s EU VAT ID.
5) Evidence: I’ve exported a short sample set that shows the duplicate pairs and the ledger trace; attaching as audit_evidence_request.pdf.

If everyone is aligned I can run the reprocess and draft the credit memo; Jordan can stage the adjustment. Expected turnaround: 3 business days once we have the legal billing entity.

-Ben
Ben Carter
